summary: People analytics and people science specialist combining employee listening, psychometrics and workplace AI insights. projects.title: Agentic AI readiness, teaming & trust
projects.summary: Analysed organisational readiness, trust and human–agent teaming in selected studies; co-author of the full four-chapter public research report.
projects.question: What evidence helps organisations understand readiness for and adoption of agentic ways of working?
projects.contribution: Led selected study analyses within the research programme, producing in-depth reports using factor analysis, regression, comparative and descriptive methods.
projects.outcome: An analytical report series and co-authorship of the full 2025 Agentic Teaming & Trust Research Report.
projects.interpretation: The public study surveyed 1,800 full-time employees across nine markets. Among agent users, leadership role-modelling was associated with higher reported value from agents (p. 15). This highlights leadership practices alongside tool access, but does not establish causality.

projects.title: Engagement drivers and attrition risk
projects.summary: Linked employee feedback and behavioural data to inform customer recommendations on engagement and attrition risk.
projects.question: Which engagement signals are associated with disengagement and attrition risk?
projects.contribution: Built linked-data analyses combining employee surveys and behavioural information; interpreted relative-risk and key-driver findings with customer-facing teams.
projects.approach: Used engagement-driver findings to frame customer engagement priorities and risk comparisons to support discussions about disengagement and attrition.
projects.outcome: Engagement-priority and retention-risk recommendations for senior customer stakeholders, informed by linked survey and behavioural data.
projects.interpretation: Risk associations identify patterns to investigate; they do not establish that changing an engagement factor will prevent attrition.

projects.title: Organisational AI-readiness measurement
projects.summary: Led the study's analysis of AI-readiness measurement and associated factors.
projects.question: Are we measuring organisational AI readiness reliably, and what factors are associated with it?
projects.contribution: Led the instrument's measurement analysis using exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, reliability testing and item analysis.
projects.approach: Examined how survey items grouped and their internal consistency before analysing readiness associations through regression, correlation and relative weight analysis.
projects.outcome: Measurement and relationship analyses referenced in The state of AI change readiness eBook.
projects.interpretation: Structure and reliability tests address aspects of measurement quality, not all forms of validity. Associated-factor analyses do not establish causal effects.

projects.title: EMEA HR shared-services satisfaction

projects.question: How can a regional HR service understand the experience it provides?
projects.contribution: Led requirements and survey design, implementation, analysis and reporting for the EMEA HR Shared Services customer-satisfaction programme.
projects.outcome: A regional survey and reporting approach, with service-improvement recommendations for HR Shared Services stakeholders.

projects.title: Early AI-assistant adoption insights
projects.summary: From the first findings report to a sustained enterprise AI survey-reporting cycle.
projects.question: What do early users tell us about adopting an enterprise AI assistant?
projects.contribution: Co-produced the first findings report as one of two analysts, monitoring responses, comparing respondent populations and reviewing data quality; then maintained recurring analysis with research partners.
projects.outcome: Initial findings and recurring reports, including quarterly reporting. Survey insights featured in public workplace research and conference presentations.
projects.interpretation: Recurring reporting is not automatically a longitudinal panel, and early-user survey responses do not on their own establish causal productivity gains.

projects.title: Post-migration NPS analysis
projects.summary: Led Net Promoter Score (NPS) survey analysis to understand customer experience following a product migration.
projects.question: How did customers experience the migration, and which themes should product teams prioritise?
projects.contribution: Led post-migration NPS survey analysis, comparing responses across roles and service models and examining group scores, satisfaction-driver patterns and correlations.
projects.approach: Used group comparisons alongside driver and correlation analyses to identify satisfaction patterns and pain points for product-team prioritisation.
projects.outcome: Prioritised customer-experience recommendations for the product teams responsible for the migrated experience.
projects.interpretation: Survey associations describe customer experience after migration, rather than isolating a causal migration effect.
